SEARCH
Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.driver

Interface DriverSession

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
@Internal public interface DriverSession extends AutoCloseable
Runs statements and transaction commands on one physical connection.

A session is not thread-safe and is used by one thread at a time. Handing a session to another thread needs a happens-before handoff, for example through an executor or a concurrent queue. Operations added in later versions arrive as default methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, so an existing driver keeps compiling.

Bound and returned values follow the values contract described in the package documentation.

Savepoint names passed to savepoint(String), rollbackToSavepoint(String) and releaseSavepoint(String) are generated by the core (as diwan_N, or diwan_N_M for a later savepoint at the same depth N) and always match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,29}, so a driver may put them into SQL unquoted. Names are unique within a session.

API Note:
Internal: driver SPI for dialect modules.
Implementation Requirements:
Implementations must report every failure as a DriverException whose kinds the driver sets, since only the driver knows its database's codes. Returned values must follow the values contract and be fully converted before the statement call returns. After any failed statement the session must stay usable, subject to the database's own rules (PostgreSQL, for example, aborts the surrounding transaction).

  • Method Details

    • query

      List<Map<String,Object>> query(String sql, List<Object> bindings)
      Runs a read and returns its rows.
      Parameters:
      sql - the statement to run, never null
      bindings - the positional parameter values, never null, elements may be null; read-only to the driver and not retained
      Returns:
      the rows in result order, never null, possibly empty
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the statement fails or a column label appears twice in the result
      Implementation Requirements:
      Rows must be in result order and each row's columns in select order, keyed by the label exactly as the database reports it. A label that appears twice in one result must fail with a DriverException with no kinds whose message names the label. The returned list and maps may be mutable; the core wraps them before handing them on.

    • cursor

      default RowCursor cursor(String sql, List<Object> bindings)
      Runs a read and streams its rows through a cursor that keeps the statement open.

      The session is busy until the cursor is closed: the core sends nothing else to it while the cursor is open.

      Parameters:
      sql - the statement to run, never null
      bindings - the positional parameter values, never null, elements may be null; read-only to the driver and not retained
      Returns:
      the open cursor, never null
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the statement fails or a column label appears twice in the result
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the driver cannot stream
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default throws UnsupportedOperationException, for drivers written before cursors. Rows follow the rules of query(java.lang.String, java.util.List<java.lang.Object>). A driver whose database streams only inside a transaction reports DriverCapability.STREAMS_IN_TRANSACTION; when no transaction is open and inExternalTransaction() is false, it opens one for the cursor and ends it when the cursor closes (commit, or rollback after a failure), restoring the session as it was. Inside a transaction the cursor reads in it and never ends it. If opening fails, everything opened so far is released before the failure is thrown.

    • inExternalTransaction

      boolean inExternalTransaction()
      Tells whether the connection was already inside a transaction Diwan Database does not own.
      Returns:
      true if an external transaction was active when the connection was acquired
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the state cannot be read
      Implementation Requirements:
      The answer describes the connection as it was acquired, before any begin() on this session, and must stay the same for the life of the session. When it is true the core never calls begin(), commit() or rollback() on this session, only the savepoint methods; a driver may throw IllegalStateException if they are called anyway.

    • begin

      void begin()
      Starts a transaction.
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the transaction cannot be started
      IllegalStateException - if inExternalTransaction() is true; optional
      Implementation Requirements:
      The connection stays inside the transaction until commit(), rollback() or close(). After commit or rollback the session may begin again.

    • lockWait

      default LockWaitGuard lockWait(long millis)
      Prepares a lock wait for the next transaction of this session.
      Parameters:
      millis - the longest wait in milliseconds, more than zero
      Returns:
      the guard that applies and removes the wait, never null
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the driver cannot limit the wait for a lock
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default throws UnsupportedOperationException, for drivers written before lock waits. The returned guard is used for one transaction: the core calls its steps around begin() and then LockWaitGuard.restore().

    • statementLockWait

      default LockWaitGuard statementLockWait(long millis)
      Prepares a limit on the wait for the locks of one statement, inside the open transaction. The limit applies to that statement only. The core calls LockWaitGuard.beforeBegin() on the guard to apply it, runs the statement, and calls LockWaitGuard.restore() to put the previous wait back, unless the statement failed. LockWaitGuard.afterBegin() is not used. Nothing is applied before beforeBegin.
      Parameters:
      millis - the longest wait in milliseconds, more than zero
      Returns:
      the guard of that one statement, never null
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the driver cannot limit the wait for a lock
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default throws UnsupportedOperationException, for drivers written before lock waits. A guard must not restore after a failed statement, because the database may have aborted the transaction; ending the transaction takes the limit back.

    • exactDecimalDigits

      default OptionalInt exactDecimalDigits()
      Tells how many significant digits the database keeps exactly in a decimal column.
      Returns:
      the number of exact significant digits, or empty when there is no such limit
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default returns empty, meaning the database keeps every digit its column type allows. A database that stores decimals as binary floating point returns the digits it keeps (SQLite: 15).

    • commit

      void commit()
      Commits the transaction begin() started.

      The core never retries a transaction whose commit failed, because the commit may have landed before the failure was reported.

      Throws:
      DriverException - if the commit fails
      IllegalStateException - if inExternalTransaction() is true; optional
      Implementation Requirements:
      After this call the session may begin() again. A driver must not classify a failure whose outcome is unknown, such as a connection lost during the commit, as DriverFailureKind.CONCURRENCY; only a commit the database definitely refused may carry that kind.

    • rollback

      void rollback()
      Rolls back the transaction begin() started.
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the rollback fails
      IllegalStateException - if inExternalTransaction() is true; optional
      Implementation Requirements:
      After this call the session may begin() again.

    • savepoint

      void savepoint(String name)
      Creates a savepoint inside the current transaction.
      Parameters:
      name - the savepoint name, never null, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,29} and unique within the session
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the savepoint cannot be created
      IllegalArgumentException - if name does not match the pattern; optional
      Implementation Requirements:
      Must work without begin() when inExternalTransaction() is true.

    • rollbackToSavepoint

      void rollbackToSavepoint(String name)
      Rolls back to a savepoint created earlier in the current transaction.
      Parameters:
      name - the savepoint name, never null, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,29}
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the rollback fails
      IllegalArgumentException - if name does not match the pattern; optional
      Implementation Requirements:
      The savepoint must remain usable afterwards: it can be rolled back to again or released. Must work without begin() when inExternalTransaction() is true.

    • releaseSavepoint

      void releaseSavepoint(String name)
      Releases a savepoint without ending the transaction.
      Parameters:
      name - the savepoint name, never null, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,29}
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the release fails
      IllegalArgumentException - if name does not match the pattern; optional
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the driver does not report DriverCapability.SAVEPOINT_RELEASE; optional
      Implementation Requirements:
      The core calls this only when Driver.info() reports DriverCapability.SAVEPOINT_RELEASE; a driver that does not report it may throw UnsupportedOperationException. Must work without begin() when inExternalTransaction() is true.

    • close

      void close()
      Ends any open transaction, restores the connection state and gives the connection back.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Throws:
      DriverException - if rolling back, restoring or giving back the connection fails
      Implementation Requirements:
      If a transaction started by begin() is still open, this method rolls it back and never commits it. It must be idempotent: a second call does nothing. It must be valid after any failure of begin(), commit(), rollback() or a statement. Restoring the connection state and giving the connection back are each attempted even if an earlier step failed; the first failure is thrown as a DriverException and later ones are attached to it with Throwable.addSuppressed(Throwable).

    • discard

      default void discard()
      Gives the connection back so that it is never handed out again.

      The core calls this instead of close() when the session may be left in a state the next user must not inherit, such as a setting it changed and could not restore.

      Throws:
      DriverException - if giving back the connection fails
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default calls close(). A driver over a pool should make the pool drop the connection. It must be idempotent, and a call after close() does nothing.
